phrases.text: So welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now, in this problem, we are given that a flight covers a total distance of one thousand
two hundred kilometer.
The speed of the flight is reduced by two hundred kilometer per hour.
Because of this reduction in speed,
the journey takes one extra hour.
The question is asking us to find the original duration of the flight.
Now, let us assume the original time taken by the flight is t hours.
Since we already know the total distance,
we can write the original speed using the formula.
Speed is equal to distance divided by time.
So original speed is equal to one thousand two hundred divided by t. After the speed is reduced, the journey takes one more hour, so the new time becomes t plus one hours.
Using the same formula,
new speed is equal to one thousand two hundred divided by t plus one.
And be very sure about one thing,
the question says the speed is reduced by two hundred kilometers per hour. So original speed minus new speed is equal to two hundred.
Putting the values,
one thousand two hundred divided by t minus one thousand two hundred divided by t plus one is equal to two hundred. After simplifying, we get t square plus t minus six is equal to zero.
After factorizing, t plus three multiplied by t minus two is equal to zero. This gives us two values,
t is equal to two or t is equal to minus three.
But time can never be negative. Hence, the original duration of the flight is two hours. Therefore, the correct answer is option
B.
